ldapSecurityForm_pinnedCertHint: Paste your internal CA's root certificate, or the domain controller's own certificate if it's self-signed. You can paste more than one certificate back to back (e.g. a root {and} the intermediate that actually signed the DC's certificate, or two DC certificates to ride out a rotation) - same concatenated-PEM convention as any CA bundle file. When set, Flare trusts {only} the certificate(s) pasted here for LDAP connections, bypassing the host's OS trust store. Leave blank to use the OS trust store (default). Get this with, e.g. {cmd} - its output already includes the full chain.

proxyAuthSecurityForm_description: Trust an identity header from a reverse proxy that already authenticates requests in front of Flare (Authelia, Authentik, oauth2-proxy, Cloudflare Access, Tailscale Serve, ...) - no separate sign-in flow, Flare just reads the header. proxyAuthSecurityForm_headerNameHint: The request header the proxy sets to the signed-in user's identity.
proxyAuthSecurityForm_trustedCidrsHint: One or more CIDR ranges, one per line - {required} to enable this method. The header above is only trusted from a caller whose own address falls inside one of these ranges, since the header itself can be spoofed by anyone who can reach Flare.Api directly.
proxyAuthSecurityForm_groupsHeaderHint: A second header carrying comma-separated group names. Leave blank to always assign Default role below.

Set this to your proxy's own sign-out URL (or the identity provider's) to send the browser there instead.

dataSourcesPage_description: Flare.Ingest speaks plain OTLP (and can pull Prometheus metrics directly) - pick where your data is coming from for a ready-to-run snippet.
dataSourceCatalog_kubernetesIntro: Run the OpenTelemetry Collector as a DaemonSet so it tails every pod's container logs and forwards them to Flare.Ingest over OTLP.
dataSourceCatalog_kubernetesStep2Body: Replace the endpoint below with wherever Flare.Ingest is reachable from inside the cluster - a Service DNS name if it runs in-cluster too, an external host:port otherwise.
dataSourceCatalog_dockerIntro: Already have an OTLP exporter in your app? Point it at Flare.Ingest with standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* environment variables - no collector needed in between.
dataSourceCatalog_dockerStep1Body: "ingest" is the service name Flare's own docker-compose.yml gives Flare.Ingest - use whatever name your Flare.Ingest container has, as long as both containers share a network.
dataSourceCatalog_dockerStep2Body: Same variables work for a container (or any process) outside the compose network - point at the published host ports instead.
dataSourceCatalog_linuxIntro: Run the OpenTelemetry Collector to tail log files (or receive OTLP from local apps) and forward everything to Flare.
dataSourceCatalog_linuxStep3Body: Wrap this in a systemd unit for anything beyond a quick test.
dataSourceCatalog_windowsIntro: Run the OpenTelemetry Collector as a local OTLP relay, or skip it entirely and point an app's own exporter straight at Flare (see Languages & Frameworks) - same protocol either way.
dataSourceCatalog_windowsStep1Body: Grab otelcol-contrib_windows_amd64.tar.gz from the OpenTelemetry Collector releases page.
dataSourceCatalog_windowsStep2Body: Receives OTLP from apps on this machine and forwards to Flare - add the contrib windowseventlog receiver alongside otlp if you also want the Windows Event Log.
dataSourceCatalog_dotnetIntro: The standard OpenTelemetry .NET SDK exports logs straight to Flare - no Flare-specific package required.
dataSourceCatalog_dotnetStep3Body: Flare ships an Aspire.Flare package that does the above for you, reading the endpoint from a connection string (e.g. .WithReference(flare) on the AppHost side) instead of a hardcoded URI.
dataSourceCatalog_pythonIntro: Zero-code instrumentation - wrap your app's start command, no source changes needed.
dataSourceCatalog_nodejsIntro: Zero-code instrumentation via the auto-instrumentations meta-package.
dataSourceCatalog_javaIntro: Zero-code instrumentation via the OpenTelemetry Java agent - attach it and set environment variables, no source changes.
dataSourceCatalog_javaStep2Heading: Run your app with it attached
dataSourceCatalog_goIntro: Go has no zero-code agent for logs yet - wire the SDK's OTLP log exporter directly.
dataSourceCatalog_goStep2Body: The Go logs SDK is newer than traces/metrics and its API has moved faster between releases - check go.opentelemetry.io/otel's own docs if this doesn't match your installed version.
dataSourceCatalog_jenkinsIntro: Jenkins doesn't speak OTLP itself - which approach fits depends on how it's deployed.
dataSourceCatalog_jenkinsStep1Body: Nothing Jenkins-specific needed - the Kubernetes/Docker items on the Platforms tab already tail container stdout/stderr and forward it as OTLP.
dataSourceCatalog_jenkinsStep2Heading: Running on a VM or bare metal?
dataSourceCatalog_jenkinsStep2Body: Same idea as the Platforms tab's Linux/Windows items - point the Collector's filelog receiver at Jenkins' own log file instead of /var/log/**/*.log (the default location varies by install: a .deb/.rpm package writes to /var/log/jenkins/jenkins.log; running the .war directly just logs to stdout, so tail wherever that's redirected to).
dataSourceCatalog_jenkinsStep3Heading: Want per-build traces instead of raw log lines?
dataSourceCatalog_jenkinsStep3Body: Jenkins' official OpenTelemetry plugin exports each pipeline run as OTel traces (one span per stage/step) via OTLP directly - no Collector needed. It's built on the OTel Java SDK, so it reads the same standard environment variables; whether it also ships build console logs (not just traces) depends on your installed plugin version's own config screen (Manage Jenkins → Configure System → OpenTelemetry).
dataSourceCatalog_ansibleIntro: A playbook run is ephemeral, not a long-running service - the community.general collection ships an OpenTelemetry callback plugin that exports each run as an OTel trace (one span per task) instead.
dataSourceCatalog_ansibleStep2Heading: Enable the callback and point it at Flare
dataSourceCatalog_ansibleStep2Body: Double-check these env var names against your installed community.general version - callback plugin configuration has shifted across releases.
dataSourceCatalog_ansibleStep3Heading: Running via AWX/Tower, or just want the raw log?
dataSourceCatalog_ansibleStep3Body: Treat it like any other Linux service and tail its log file instead - see the Platforms tab.
dataSourceCatalog_terraformIntro: A terraform apply run is even more ephemeral than a playbook, and the CLI has no OTLP exporter of its own - get its debug log onto disk, then forward that.
dataSourceCatalog_terraformStep1Heading: Turn on Terraform's own debug log
dataSourceCatalog_terraformStep2Body: Tail terraform.log the same way the Platforms tab's Linux item tails any other log file - point the Collector's filelog receiver at it.
dataSourceCatalog_terraformStep3Heading: In ephemeral CI (e.g. a GitHub-hosted runner)
dataSourceCatalog_terraformStep3Body: There's no host left for a Collector to read from once the job ends - see the GitHub Actions item for shipping a run's outcome directly from the workflow instead.
dataSourceCatalog_githubActionsIntro: No native OTLP exporter for Actions - the reliable option is a workflow step that ships the job's outcome directly, the same shape as the Custom tab's raw curl example.
dataSourceCatalog_githubActionsStep1Body: Treat the runner like any other Linux/Windows host - see the Platforms tab. Nothing GitHub-specific needed.
dataSourceCatalog_githubActionsStep2Body: The runner disappears once the job ends, so add a step that reports the outcome directly instead, using GitHub's own workflow context. This is a minimal example (one log event per run) - free-text values like a commit message would need real JSON escaping (e.g. via jq) before going in the body.
dataSourceCatalog_vectorIntro: Vector ships a native OpenTelemetry sink - point it at Flare.Ingest directly, no separate Collector needed.
dataSourceCatalog_vectorStep1Body: inputs should list whatever source or transform is already producing the events you want shipped - a file source tailing a log, a docker_logs source, etc.
dataSourceCatalog_fluentBitIntro: Fluent Bit ships a built-in OpenTelemetry output plugin - point it at Flare.Ingest directly, no separate Collector needed.
dataSourceCatalog_syslogIntro: Flare.Ingest has no syslog listener of its own - route through the OpenTelemetry Collector's syslog receiver instead, same pattern as any other source that doesn't speak OTLP.
dataSourceCatalog_syslogStep1Body: Runs alongside whatever else the Collector is already doing on this host - see the Platforms tab for the full install steps (this is just the receiver/exporter pair to add to that config).
dataSourceCatalog_syslogStep2Body: Point whatever's emitting syslog (a network device, syslog-ng, journald's syslog forwarding, etc.) at this host on port 5514 instead of wherever it was going before.
dataSourceCatalog_prometheusIntro: The only pull-based source on this page - Flare.Ingest scrapes a Prometheus-style /metrics endpoint itself on a timer, instead of something exporting to Flare. No exporter, sidecar, or Collector needed on the target's side.
dataSourceCatalog_prometheusStep1Body: Add this to Flare.Ingest's configuration (appsettings.json, or an appsettings.Production.json override) and restart it - Job becomes the service.name every point from this target is tagged with, matching the OTel Collector's own prometheusreceiver convention.
dataSourceCatalog_prometheusStep2Body: Same shape, no file to mount - .NET's standard double-underscore config-key binding reaches the same array/object structure. "ingest" is Flare's own docker-compose.yml service name; the target itself just needs to be reachable from that container's network.
dataSourceCatalog_prometheusStep3Body: Headers are sent on every scrape request (e.g. a bearer token). Labels are merged onto every point's resource attributes, applied after - and able to override - the computed service.name/service.instance.id.
dataSourceCatalog_prometheusStep4Body: Give it one scrape interval, then look for the target's metric names on the Metrics page, or watch the "Prometheus scrape" row on the Ingestion page's Receivers table for real request counts.
dataSourceCatalog_kafkaIntro: Send your .NET producers' and consumers' Kafka spans to Flare, plus consumer lag from the OpenTelemetry Collector. Together they fill the Messaging page: publish and consume rates, errors, latency and lag per topic.
dataSourceCatalog_kafkaStep2Heading: Build clients with the instrumented builders
dataSourceCatalog_kafkaStep2Body: Pass the same builder instances to the tracer and use them to build your clients. Clients built with the plain Confluent builders emit no spans, and the builders need a ProducerConfig/ConsumerConfig object, not a plain key/value list.
dataSourceCatalog_kafkaStep3Body: Consumer lag isn't in spans. Run the OpenTelemetry Collector (contrib distribution) with the kafkametrics receiver pointed at your brokers. Collector 0.161 and later call it kafka_metrics; the old name still works.
dataSourceCatalog_kafkaStep4Body: Produce and consume a few messages, then open Messaging in the top nav. Each topic appears within a few seconds; lag appears after one collection interval.
dataSourceCatalog_rabbitmqIntro: Send your .NET publishers' and consumers' RabbitMQ spans to Flare, plus queue depth from the OpenTelemetry Collector. Together they fill the Messaging page: publish and consume rates, errors, latency and backlog per exchange or queue.
dataSourceCatalog_rabbitmqStep1Body: RabbitMQ.Client 7 and later emit OpenTelemetry spans themselves, so no separate instrumentation package is needed. Version 6 emits none.
dataSourceCatalog_rabbitmqStep2Heading: Listen to the client's activity sources
dataSourceCatalog_rabbitmqStep2Body: Add the RabbitMQ.Client activity sources to the tracer. Rows are named after the exchange you publish to. Messages sent through the default exchange appear under their queue name.
dataSourceCatalog_rabbitmqStep3Body: Queue depth isn't in spans. Run the OpenTelemetry Collector (contrib distribution) with the rabbitmq receiver. It reads the management API, so enable the rabbitmq_management plugin and create a user with the monitoring tag. The built-in guest user only works from localhost.
dataSourceCatalog_rabbitmqStep4Body: Publish and consume a few messages, then open Messaging in the top nav. Each exchange or queue appears within a few seconds; the backlog appears after one collection interval when a queue name matches the row or one of its routing keys.
dataSourceCatalog_masstransitIntro: Send MassTransit's built-in spans to Flare. They fill the Messaging page: publish and consume rates, errors and latency per message type, whichever transport you run (RabbitMQ, Azure Service Bus, ActiveMQ).
dataSourceCatalog_masstransitStep1Body: MassTransit 8 is Apache licensed and emits OpenTelemetry spans itself, so no instrumentation package is needed. MassTransit 9 is commercial and needs a license key; this guide was verified on 8.5 over RabbitMQ.
dataSourceCatalog_masstransitStep2Body: Add the MassTransit source to the tracer. MassTransit sets messaging.system on send spans only, so Flare takes the system and destination from MassTransit's endpoint address; no processor is needed.
dataSourceCatalog_masstransitStep3Body: Publish and consume a few messages, then open Messaging in the top nav. Each message type appears as one row named after the exchange it is published to, with producers and consumers together. Faults appear under a MassTransit:Fault row. The backlog column stays empty because the queue's name differs from the row's.
dataSourceCatalog_servicebusIntro: Send the Azure SDK's Service Bus spans to Flare. They fill the Messaging page: publish and consume rates, latency and errors per queue or topic.
dataSourceCatalog_servicebusStep1Body: Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus emits OpenTelemetry spans itself, so no instrumentation package is needed.
dataSourceCatalog_servicebusStep2Heading: Enable and listen to the SDK's tracing
dataSourceCatalog_servicebusStep2Body: The SDK keeps its tracing behind an experimental switch; without it no spans are emitted. Turn the switch on, then add the Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus activity sources to the tracer.
dataSourceCatalog_servicebusStep3Body: Send and process a few messages, then open Messaging in the top nav. Each queue or topic appears as one row. A batched send counts once per call, and a handler that throws isn't flagged as an error by the SDK, so the consume error count stays at 0.
dataSourceCatalog_natsIntro: Send NATS.Net's spans to Flare, plus JetStream consumer backlog from the OpenTelemetry Collector. Together they fill the Messaging page: publish and consume rates, errors, latency and backlog per subject.
dataSourceCatalog_natsStep1Body: NATS.Net 2 and later emit OpenTelemetry spans themselves, so no instrumentation package is needed.
dataSourceCatalog_natsStep2Heading: Listen to the client's activity source
dataSourceCatalog_natsStep2Body: Add the NATS.Net source to the tracer. Flare leaves out the client's own traffic (JetStream API calls, per-message acks and temporary reply inboxes), so rows are your application's subjects.
dataSourceCatalog_natsStep3Body: Backlog isn't in spans. Run prometheus-nats-exporter next to the server with -jsz=all, and scrape it with the OpenTelemetry Collector's prometheus receiver. Core NATS subscriptions have no backlog.
dataSourceCatalog_natsStep4Body: Publish and consume a few messages, then open Messaging in the top nav. Each subject appears within a few seconds. The backlog appears after one scrape interval, on subjects a JetStream consumer reads from.
dataSourceCatalog_customIntro: Flare.Ingest speaks plain OTLP - point any OTLP-capable exporter, collector, or HTTP client at it directly.
dataSourceCatalog_customStep2Body: Expect a 200 response with an empty body. The event is buffered for a couple seconds before it lands in ClickHouse, so give Logs a moment before checking.
dataSourceCatalog_customStep3Heading: If this deployment requires an ingest key
dataSourceCatalog_customStep3Body: Anonymous ingest is the default. If yours has been turned to required, create a key from an Admin session and send it as a Bearer token on every export.

Space aggregation then adds the series' increases together - what a chart grouped by an attribute shows. Rate mode divides each bucket by its width.

llmPage_hint: Rows are grouped by provider and model. The model is gen_ai.request.model (else gen_ai.response.model); tokens are summed from gen_ai.usage.input_tokens and output_tokens. Estimated cost uses built-in list prices that an admin can override per model.
llmPage_priceHint: USD, for everyone. Used to estimate cost from the token counts; cached or discounted tokens aren't visible, so treat it as an upper-bound estimate.
runtimeHealth_description: Problems found in this service's System.Runtime metrics over the last {minutes} minutes.
runtimeHealth_noData: This service sent no .NET runtime metrics in this window. Add the System.Runtime meter (.NET 9 or later) to get findings here.
runtimeHealth_detailThreadPoolStarvation: The queue grew to {peak} items while completed work items flatlined (usually {baseline}/s).
The queue grew to {peak} items while completed work items flatlined.
runtimeHealth_detailGcPressure: Up to {percent} of wall-clock time was spent paused in garbage collection.
runtimeHealth_detailLockContention: Up to {rate}/s lock contentions, against a usual {baseline}/s.
runtimeHealth_detailExceptionRate: Up to {rate}/s exceptions, against a usual {baseline}/s.
versionComparison_noVersions: No service.version resource attribute seen on this service's spans in the last {hours} hours. Set service.version on the service to compare deploys.
versionComparison_oneVersion: Only version {version} was seen in the last {hours} hours, so there is nothing to compare it with yet.
versionComparison_description: Compared over the last {hours} hours. New means seen under the current version and never under the baseline.
versionComparison_endpointsEmpty: Neither version served any endpoint in this window.
sloPage_description: Reliability targets over your services' entry spans, with the error budget they leave and burn-rate alerts that page before it runs out.
sloPage_emptyDescription: Define an availability or latency objective for a service or one of its endpoints, e.g. 99.5% of requests succeed over 28 days.
sloPage_deleteConfirm: Delete the SLO "{name}"? Its burn-rate alert rules are kept but will stop evaluating.
sloForm_kindHintAvailability: A request is good unless its span ended in an error.
sloForm_kindHintLatency: A request is good when it finishes within the threshold.
sloForm_operationHint: An entry span name such as a route. Leave empty to cover every entry span of the service.
sloForm_thresholdHint: Thresholds are fixed steps - the pre-aggregated data keeps one counter per step.
sloForm_errorTarget: The target must be between 1 and 99.999.
sloDetail_noData: No requests in this window yet. SLOs read the per-minute pre-aggregate, which only holds spans ingested since it was created - see the SLO guide for back-filling history.
sloDetail_burnRatesHint: 1x spends exactly the budget over the whole window; 14.4x spends 2% of a 30-day budget in an hour.
sloDetail_alertsHint: Rules that fire when the budget is burning fast over a long and a short window at once, sent through your notification channels.
sloDetail_presetDescription: {name}: {rate}x over {long} and {short} - {percent}% of the budget gone
sloDetail_noChannels: No notification channels yet - create one on the Alerts page first.
alertTransfer_exportTitle: Download the rules shown (all rules when no filter is active) as JSON
alertTransfer_importTitle: Import alert rules from a JSON export
alertTransfer_dialogDescription: Channels and SLOs are matched by name. Rules whose name already exists are skipped.
settingsAppearance_description: How Flare looks and where things are on screen.
settingsAppearance_navTopDescription: Page links in a bar across the top.
settingsAppearance_navSidebarDescription: A vertical menu on the left that can shrink to icons.
settingsAppearance_sidebarCollapsedDescr: Gives pages more room. You can also toggle it from the sidebar itself.
settingsAppearance_densityCompactDescrip: Tighter rows, more data on screen.
settingsAppearance_previewHint: Updates as you change a setting
settingsAppearance_storageNote: These settings are saved to your account and also cached in this browser.
settingsAppearance_contentWidthFullDescr: Pages stretch to fill the window.
settingsAppearance_contentWidthCenteredD: Pages are capped at a readable width on large screens.
settingsAppearance_monoLogsDescription: Show log bodies in a monospace font.
settingsAppearance_sidebarHoverExpandDes: Float the collapsed sidebar open while the pointer is over it.
settingsRegional_description: Language and time zone. The user menu keeps these as shortcuts.
settingsRegional_timeZoneDescription: Timestamps across the dashboard are shown in this zone.
settingsRegional_weekStartDescription: Used by the "This week" time range.
settingsRegional_defaultRangeDescription: The time range each explorer opens with.
settingsRegional_defaultRangeNote: Applies the next time the page loads; saved views and links keep their own range.
settingsKeyboard_description: Every shortcut in one place. Click a binding, then press the keys you want. Changes sync to your account.
settingsKeyboard_action_nextEvent: Next log event (while details are open)
settingsKeyboard_action_prevEvent: Previous log event (while details are open)
settingsKeyboard_fixed_closeDialog: Close a dialog, sheet or palette
settingsKeyboard_fixed_stepEvents: Step between events in the side panel
settingsExplorer_description: Where the explorers start. Saved views and shared links keep their own values, and changes apply the next time a page loads.
settingsExplorer_landingDescription: Where the bare address opens. Default keeps your home dashboard if you set one, otherwise Logs.
settingsExplorer_rowClick: When I click a log row
settingsExplorer_rowClickHint: Inline expansion keeps the list in view. Use j/k to step between rows.
settingsExplorer_bucketNote: A width too fine for a long range is raised automatically.
settingsExplorer_facetOpen: Start with the facet sidebar open
settingsExplorer_pinnedDescription: Shown first in the event and span detail sheets. These are stored in this browser only.
settingsExplorer_liveAutoScroll: Auto-scroll to the newest row while live-tailing
settingsExplorer_storedDescription: Small conveniences that live only in this browser. Clearing one never touches your saved views or dashboards.
settingsExplorer_clearCollapsed: Reset collapsed filter rows and charts
settingsNotifications_description: Choose which notices Flare shows you. Changes sync to your account.
settingsNotifications_updateNoticeHint: The version line in the user menu stays either way.
settingsNotifications_browserHint: A notification appears when an alert rule fires while a Flare tab is open. Permission is granted per browser.
settingsNotifications_browserUnsupported: This browser does not support notifications.
settingsNotifications_browserDenied: Notifications are blocked for this site in your browser settings.
settingsNotifications_emailNote: Alert emails go to the recipients configured on each notification channel, so there is no per-user opt-out; edit the channel to change who receives them.
mcpConnect_description: Flare exposes a read-only MCP endpoint at {url}. Create a token below and register it with Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code.
userInvite_description: Creates a local account and a one-time link the person uses to choose their password. The link expires and works once.
userInvite_linkHint: Share this link securely. It is shown only once and expires {expires}.
userInvite_emailed: We also emailed this link to {username}.
userInvite_bulkHint: Add several at once: one username per line, or separated by commas.
userInvite_bulkHintResult: Links are shown only once and expire {expires}. Copy them before closing.
setPassword_description: Choose a password for your Flare account.
setPassword_tooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters.
setPassword_invalid: This link is invalid or has expired. Ask an admin for a new one.
setPassword_success: Password set. You can now sign in.
setPassword_missingToken: This link is missing its token.
settingsSessions_description: Browsers and devices currently signed in to your account.
settingsExport_description: Download your saved views and the dashboards you own as a JSON file.
settingsPrefsBackup_description: Download your display preferences (appearance, regional, explorer, keyboard, notifications) as a JSON file, or restore them from one. Importing overwrites matching settings and reloads the page.
settingsAccount_description: Your other signed-in sessions are signed out; this one stays.
settingsAccount_tooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters.
projectsPage_description: A project is a named set of services plus the people who may see them. Members see only their projects' services, dashboards, alerts, SLOs and views.
projectsPage_emptyDescription: Until a project exists, everyone sees every service. Creating the first one restricts non-admin users to the projects they belong to.
projectsPage_confirmDelete: Delete project "{name}"? Its dashboards, alerts, SLOs, views and ingest keys become visible to global admins only until reassigned.
projectForm_description: Scope a project to the services it owns.
projectForm_patternsHint: One service.name per line. A trailing * matches a prefix (checkout-*). A bare * is not allowed.
projectMembers_description: A member's project role only narrows their global role: a global Viewer can't edit even as a project Member.
projectMembers_empty: No members yet. Non-admin users outside every project see nothing.
projectPicker_hint: Only members of the project can see or change this.
moveIngestKeyDialog_description: Ownership only: what the key may ingest doesn't change.
ackRule_ackHint: Stops re-notifications until the alert resolves.
oncall_description: Named rotations of notification channels that take turns being on call. An alert rule can escalate to whoever is on call.
oncall_emptyDescription: Create a rotation, then pick it in an alert rule's escalation settings.
oncall_deleteConfirm: Delete the rotation "{name}"? Rules that escalate to it fall back to their fixed escalation channels.
oncall_participantsHint: Each participant is a notification channel (a person's email or chat, or a team channel). The list repeats after the last one.
oncall_startsHint: The first participant is on call from here. Shown in your browser's time zone.
oncall_errorShift: Shift length must be between 1 and 8760 hours.
oncall_overridesHint: A one-off swap: this channel is on call for the period instead of the scheduled participant. Shown in your browser's time zone.
oncall_errorOverrides: Each override needs a channel and an end after its start.
oncall_coverageHint: Outside this window nobody on the rotation is paged; the rule's fixed escalation channels and overrides still are. An end earlier than the start runs past midnight.
oncall_errorCoverage: Pick at least one day, a known time zone, and different start and end times.
ackLink_description: Confirm that you are handling this alert. Re-notifications stop until it resolves.
ackLink_done: Acknowledged. Re-notifications for this incident have stopped.
ackLink_invalid: This link is invalid or has expired. Open the alert in Flare to acknowledge it.
ackLink_notFiring: This alert is no longer firing, so there is nothing to acknowledge.
ackLink_missingToken: This link is missing its token.
synthetic_description: Scheduled HTTP, TCP and TLS probes. Results are stored as synthetic.* metrics, so metric alerts and dashboards work on them.
synthetic_emptyDescription: Create a monitor to probe an endpoint, a port or a certificate, then alert on the synthetic.up metric.
synthetic_headersHint: One per line, Name: value. Values are hidden after saving; keep ******** to leave one unchanged.
synthetic_jsonAssertionHint: Optional. Regex uses a linear-time engine: no lookarounds or backreferences. Optional. Path like $.data.items[0].status; leave the value empty to only require the path to exist.
synthetic_locationsHint: Comma-separated names of workers that run this monitor (each worker's Synthetic__Location). Empty means every location.
synthetic_locationsError: Up to 20 names of letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-'.
synthetic_deleteConfirm: Delete the monitor "{name}"? Its metrics stop being reported.
synthetic_targetHintHttp: An absolute http or https URL.
synthetic_targetHintTcp: host:port. Up when the connection opens.
synthetic_targetHintTls: host or host:port (443 by default). Also records days until the certificate expires.
synthetic_targetHintDns: A domain name or IP address. Up when it resolves.
synthetic_targetHintUdp: host:port. Up when a reply datagram arrives.
synthetic_targetHintIcmp: A host name or IP address. Up when an ICMP echo is answered.
synthetic_expectedAddressLabel: Answer must include (IP for A/AAAA, text otherwise)
synthetic_udpHint: UDP has no handshake: with no reply within the timeout the monitor is down, so use it only for services that always answer.
synthetic_expectedStatusHint: 0 counts any 2xx or 3xx response as up.
synthetic_errorInterval: Interval must be between 10 and 86400 seconds.
synthetic_errorTimeout: Timeout must be between 1 and 120 seconds and not above the interval.
statusPages_description: Publish a read-only page of monitor and SLO health that anyone with the link can open, no sign-in needed.
statusPages_emptyDescription: Group synthetic monitors and SLOs into a page you can share with customers or teammates.
statusPages_deleteConfirm: Delete the status page "{title}"? Its link stops working immediately.
statusPages_formDescription: Visitors see only the title, the component names you choose and their state. Monitor targets and SLO names are never shown.
statusPages_slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. The page is served at /status/<slug>.
statusPages_componentsHint: A monitor shows up or down from its latest probes. An SLO shows operational until its error budget is spent.
statusPages_subscribersHint: Each channel is told when an incident is opened or updated on this page. Webhook, Slack, Telegram, email, Teams and Discord channels only.
statusPages_noChannels: Create a webhook, Telegram, email, Teams or Discord notification channel first.
statusSubscribe_sent: Check your inbox: we sent a link to confirm this address.
statusSubscribe_hint: You will be emailed when an incident is opened or updated. Every email has an unsubscribe link.
statusSubscribe_componentsAll: Leave all unticked to hear about every component, or tick the ones you care about.
statusSubscribe_componentsSome: Only incidents affecting the ticked components. Incidents that name no component always reach you.
statusSubscribe_confirmed: Done. {email} will get incident updates about {page}.
statusSubscribe_unsubscribePrompt: Stop sending incident updates about {page} to {email}?
statusSubscribe_unsubscribed: Done. {email} will no longer get incident updates about {page}.
statusSubscribe_missingToken: This link is missing its token.
statusSubscribe_preferencesPrompt: Choose which components of {page} to email {email} about. Leave all unticked to hear about every component.
statusSubscribe_preferencesSaved: Saved. {email} will get incident updates about {page} for the ticked components, and for any incident that names no component.
statusPages_domainHint: Optional. Also serve this page on your own host. Point its DNS and TLS at the dashboard first; that host then shows only this page.
statusPages_noSources: Create a synthetic monitor or an SLO first.
statusPages_publicWarning: Anyone who can reach this instance can read this page without signing in.
statusPublic_notFound: This status page does not exist.
statusPublic_historyLabel: Daily uptime for the last {days} days
statusIncidents_description: Written updates appear on the public page while an incident is open and for 14 days after it resolves.
statusIncidents_deleteConfirm: Delete the incident "{title}" and its updates? It disappears from the public page.
alertRuleForm_quorumHint: Picking a number sets Last below a threshold on the fraction of locations that see the monitor up.
alertRuleForm_secondEscalateMinutes: minutes after the first escalation, notify
alertRuleForm_secondEscalateInvalid: Choose a delay between 1 and 10080 minutes and at least one channel.
createLogMetricButton_hint: Count the logs matching this search as a metric
logMetricTable_subheading: Count matching logs at ingest and store the counts as a metric you can chart and alert on.
logMetricTable_emptyDescription: A log metric counts the logs matching a filter as they arrive, so charts and alerts read a metric instead of scanning logs.
logMetricTable_deleteConfirm: Delete log metric "{name}"? New points stop; stored points stay until they age out.
logMetricForm_description: Counts start when the metric is saved; nothing is backfilled from stored logs.
logMetricForm_metricNameHint: Letters, digits, _ . - ; start with a letter. A logs. prefix keeps it apart from real metrics.
logMetricForm_carriedOver: Also filtering on: {fields} (carried over from the search).
logMetricForm_matchesAllLogsWarning: No filter set: this metric counts every log.
logMetricForm_groupByHint: Each key splits the metric into one series per value (at most {max}). Keep them low-cardinality.
logMetricForm_previewNoMatches: No matching logs in the last {minutes} min
logMetricForm_previewLogs: from {logs} logs in the last {minutes} min
profilesPage_noTypes: No profiles in this window. Send OTLP profiles to Flare (see the continuous profiling docs).
profilesPage_truncated: Truncated: the lightest stacks are not shown
profilesPage_hint: Click a frame to zoom into it
profilesPage_noStacks: These samples carry no call stacks, so there is no flame graph to draw. Check that your sender includes stack data.
schedule_description: Email this dashboard as a PDF or PNG on a schedule. It is rendered with your access when it runs.
schedule_empty: No schedules yet. Create one to email this dashboard to a team on a cadence.
schedule_sendNowQueued: "{name}" is queued and goes out within a minute. Check its run history for the result.
schedule_cronHint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. Read in the time zone below.
schedule_recipientsHint: Comma-separated email addresses. Reports go out through the server's SMTP settings.
retentionPage_intro: How long each signal is kept. Changes are applied by ClickHouse in the background and only affect how data is deleted or moved, never how it is written.
retention_coldUnavailable: Cold storage isn't configured on this ClickHouse. Start Flare with docker-compose.cold-storage.yml (or WithColdStorage() in Aspire) to tier old data to object storage.
retention_actualCustom: Custom TTL not set by Flare
retention_zeroHint: 0 means keep forever (for cold storage: no tiering).
retention_rulesHint: Rows whose resource attribute equals the value use that retention instead of the default. The first matching rule wins.
retention_invalidDays: Days must be a whole number from 0 to {max}.
retention_ruleIncomplete: Every rule needs an attribute and a value.
retention_coldTooLate: Cold-after must be less than the shortest retention ({days}d), or data would be deleted before it moves.
alertTemplates_description: Named, reusable wording for alert notifications. A rule picks a template; editing it updates every rule that uses it. The default template applies to rules that pick none.
alertTemplates_emptyDescription: Alerts use each channel's built-in wording until you create a template and pick it on a rule, or mark one as the default.
alertTemplates_deleteConfirm: Delete the template "{name}"? A template that rules still use can't be deleted.
alertTemplateForm_defaultHint: Applies to every rule that doesn't pick a template. Only one template can be the default.
alertTemplateForm_resolvedHint: Optional. Used for resolved notifications; empty reuses the fired body.
alertTemplateForm_channelBodiesHint: Optional. Replaces the fired body for one channel type, e.g. a short text for Telegram. Other channel types use the fired body.
alertRuleForm_sharedTemplateHint: A shared template from Settings. The text you write below still overrides it.
sourceMaps_description: Maps uploaded by CI with flare sourcemaps upload. Flare uses them to translate minified browser stack traces on the Errors page, matched by service, version and script path.
sourceMaps_emptyDescription: Upload a map per bundle from your build: flare sourcemaps upload --service web --version 1.4.2 dist/assets
sourceMaps_confirmDeleteRelease: Delete all source maps of {service} {version}? Stack traces from that release will show minified again.
frontendPage_vitalsDescription: 75th percentile per service over the window, coloured against Google's thresholds. The percentage is the share of measurements the browser rated good.
frontendPage_noVitals: No browser.web_vital.* metrics in this window.
frontendPage_errorsDescription: Exceptions from services whose SDK language is webjs, grouped by type and message.
frontendPage_noErrors: No browser errors in this window.
frontendPage_emptyTitle: No browser telemetry in this window
frontendPage_emptyDescription: Send Core Web Vitals as browser.web_vital.* histograms and JavaScript errors as spans with an exception event from the OpenTelemetry JS SDK.
frontendPage_noRoutes: No url.template attribute on these vitals, so there is no per-route breakdown.
telemetryExport_intro: Copy telemetry out of Flare: forward it to other OTLP endpoints as it is ingested, or archive it hourly to S3-compatible storage. Settings saved here apply without a restart and take precedence over configuration files.
telemetryExport_signalsHint: Leave all unchecked to include logs, traces and metrics.
telemetryExport_fwdIntro: Accepted OTLP requests are queued in Redis per target and delivered at least once. Targets defined in configuration are listed read-only.
telemetryExport_fwdDeleteConfirm: Delete the forwarding target "{name}"? Requests still queued for it are discarded.
telemetryExport_fwdEndpointHint: OTLP/HTTP base URL; /v1/logs, /v1/traces and /v1/metrics are appended.
telemetryExport_fwdHeadersHint: One "Name: value" per line. Saved values are hidden; leave a hidden value as it is to keep it.
telemetryExport_fwdServicesHint: Comma-separated service.name values. Empty forwards every service; other services' data is removed from the copy.
telemetryExport_fwdKeysHint: Forward only requests authenticated with the checked keys. Empty forwards every request.
telemetryExport_archiveIntro: Hourly export of finished ingest hours to S3-compatible storage as Parquet or NDJSON. ClickHouse writes the files directly.
telemetryExport_archiveUsingConfig: No saved settings: following the worker's configuration.
telemetryExport_archiveEndpointHint: Path-style URL of the bucket, e.g. http://rustfs:9000/flare-archive.
telemetryExport_archiveKeysHint: Saved keys are hidden; leave them as they are to keep them.
telemetryExport_archiveSaved: Saved. The archive picks this up on its next poll.
telemetryExport_archiveResetConfirm: Discard the saved archive settings and follow the worker's configuration again?
telemetryExport_archiveResetDone: Reset. The archive follows the configuration again.
usage_intro: What is driving storage: volume per service and ingest key, and the largest attributes. Use it before choosing sampling or retention rules.
usage_servicesNote: On-disk size is an estimate: each signal's compressed table size split by the service's share of events in the window.
usage_keysNote: Accepted volume in the current UTC day (the only window the per-key counters keep).
usage_attributesNote: Key and value bytes (uncompressed) in a sample of up to {rows} recent rows per source. Share is within the same source.
sessionsPage_emptyDescription: Sessions are spans that share a session.id attribute. Flare.Maui sets one per app launch; other SDKs can add it to their spans.
sessionsPage_truncated: Showing the most recent 500 sessions; narrow the window or filters to see the rest.
sessionsPage_hint: A session is one app launch. Open a session to see its traces, in order.
sessionsPage_detail_empty: No spans for this session in the time range. It may be older than the range in the link.
sessionsPage_detail_truncated: Showing the first 1,000 spans of this session.
sessionsPage_health_hint: A session crashed when the app reported a fatal unhandled exception. Users are counted from the user.id attribute and show a dash when the app sets none.
